speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle and now have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with pain during urination. To understand what is causing these symptoms, have you noticed any fever, chills, or rash accompanying the joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle, now knee), urethritis (pain with urination), recent onset in a sexually active young male, and the classic triad of symptoms is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis. I will order specific tests to confirm the etiology and rule out other causes.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Chlamydia PCR (Urine), HLA-B27, ESR, CRP.
